methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $10M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Signaloid is a Seed-stage semiconductor company that has raised $10M to date. The valuation universe includes 11 peers in the Chips & Semiconductors sector—3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent. However, comparable company analysis proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and similar-tier peers within the semiconductor space; fewer than three narrow comparables could be identified.

Consequently, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using $10M in total raised as a value proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement in venture capital, the analysis yields an implied valuation of $25M. This single-method approach produced a triangulated range of $21M (low) to $29M (high), centered on a $25M median.

The valuation estimate is materially constrained by limited peer data in the semiconductor sector at comparable stages and scales. Key uncertainties include the applicability of standard 2.5x stage multipliers to deep-tech hardware companies, which may exhibit different risk-return profiles than software or services peers. Additional clarity on Signaloid's technical differentiation, IP position, and path to revenue would strengthen conviction in this range. The range should be treated as indicative pending comparable transaction or market data in frontier semiconductor ventures.
